text: BRD Program v4 and BRD Epic 1 v4 are taken as the approved business baseline for this PRD even though neither carries a status field or an approval record, so the PRD is issued as Draft with an empty approval table and the requirements approval gate stays open.
why: Neither BRD document control table has a status or an approval row (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-10), and the realignment run does not stop for a missing approval.
read: Business requirements Program v4 and Epic 1 v4, version 4 dated 15 November 2026, are the baseline; the PRD approval is pending.
applied_in: Section 1 document control, section 13 approval table
confirm: Product Owner and FDA at the requirements approval gate
impact: The PRD is a Draft baseline; no story is blocked because the story set already exists.

text: The product baseline of this PRD is BRD Program v4 section 5.2 and section 6, BRD Epic 1 v4 section 3.2, FSD P2 Integration v3 (the latest FSD of the family), Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 and the Ownership Map; the Story Template and Rules v1 supplies the precedence rule, the DP table and the R9 placeholder.
why: No earlier PRD exists in the family and the source set names several versions; the highest version of each family is the one this run reads.
read: FSD P2 Integration v3 dated 15 November 2026 is the source of the functional detail; Arch v5 wins over it where they disagree (R-PREC rule 1).
impact: A later FSD version re-baselines the FR table.

text: Architecture v5 wins on the data lake: legacy INT-19 is a delivery request raised by rwb-reporting and carried by rwb-integration, legacy INT-20 is continuous DecisionRecorded ingest in rwb-decision, no lake target, lake file, lake copy or lake delivery row exists, and JOB-13 and JOB-15 are not P2 schedules.
why: Architecture v5 slides 7, 8, 13 and 44 and DP-17 remove the data lake; FSD P2 v3 still lists the two lake adapters (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-1).
read: Precedence R-PREC rule 1 puts the Arch v5 catalogue above the FSD; the loser is recorded as a gap and an assumption.
applied_in: Section 2, section 5 CAP-P2-003, section 6 FR-P2-005, section 9 integration points
impact: BRD Program v4 section 5.2 and the FSD A1.5 need the same correction in their next versions.

text: Only rwb-source-data reads the thirty recovery.v_ace_* views; every ACE fact an outbound file or the hand-over needs is read through the rwb-source-data contract, one hop with a 2 s budget, and the rwb_integration login holds no grant on the recovery schema and no grant on another rwb_* schema.
why: Architecture v5 slides 8, 9, 13, 29 and 37, ADR-010 and DP-05 reserve the views to rwb-source-data, while the FSD has the outbound file read them (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-2).
read: The FSD sentences that name v_ace_contact, v_ace_batch_status and v_ace_account are the legacy wording of the file build; the data arrives through the owner's contract.
applied_in: Section 2 constraints, section 6 FR-P2-018, section 8 data requirements, section 9
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-source-data owner
impact: A read grant on the views would break the service boundary and the architecture test.

text: Job ownership follows the Ownership Map: JOB-10 WIN notices belongs to P6 rwb-comms with rwb-integration building and delivering the file, JOB-11 outbox sender belongs to the platform library, JOB-13 to P7 rwb-decision as continuous ingest and JOB-15 to P9 rwb-reporting; rwb-integration registers no Temporal Schedule and owns no scheduled job.
why: The FSD places the three jobs inside P2 while the Ownership Map and Arch v5 slide 44 place them with their owning services (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-3).
read: P2 provides the delivery capability, the item lifecycle, the retry ladder inside a window and the two events; the schedule and the business trigger stay with the owner of the business step.
impact: The operations story of the service carries no Schedule; an added Schedule would break the Ownership Map.

text: The transfer window and the re-run of a window belong to the bank scheduler, and the attempt ladder inside the window, the exception state, the owner task and the resend belong to the service; the single owner of a retry count is open under DL11.
why: Arch v5 slide 32 gives Airflow the window, the transfer and the retry, while the FSD gives the service three attempts and an exception queue (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-4).
read: Both duties are stated as requirements; the product baseline does not pick one of them as the only retry owner.
confirm: Solution architect with the IT lead
impact: A duplicate retry would send a file twice; the acceptance criterion on replay guards it.

text: FileDelivered and FileFailed are P2's own events on rwb.integration.events.v1, keyed by case ID, with no numbered EV ID in the sources; the event name form is rwb.integration.<Event>.v1 under the naming rule of Template and Rules section R4.
why: Arch v5 slide 43 gives the two events to rwb-integration and the Ownership Map has no row for them (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-5).
read: The two events are the service's only published events; the shared DecisionRecorded event is published by the decision-record library and belongs to P7.
impact: A missing row would leave the service's events without an owner in the register.

text: The INT-25 tape rows, the account keys and the sale terms travel in the delivery request manifest raised by rwb-debtsale, and the account facts are read through the rwb-source-data contract; rwb-integration reads neither debt_sale_account nor an ACE view.
why: The Ownership Map gives debt_sale_account to S6 rwb-debtsale and the views to P1, and DP-01 forbids a cross-schema read (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-6).
read: The FSD sentence that builds the tape from debt_sale_account is superseded; the manifest carries the keys.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-debtsale owner
impact: The tape is built from the request, so a missing key fails the request and not the read.

text: Retry counts and intervals are interface configuration rows with the version in force (max attempts 3; intervals 5, 15 and 45 minutes in interface version IF-2026.11); the product baseline states the FSD behaviour as the acceptance criterion, that attempt 2 follows attempt 1 by 5 minutes and attempt 3 follows attempt 2 by 15 minutes, and fixes neither number as a product rule.
why: The FSD criterion and the interface configuration disagree on the third interval and no source resolves it (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-7).
read: A change of the numbers is a data load and not a release.
confirm: Platform administrator with the reference data administrator
impact: A changed row changes the behaviour of every interface that shares it.

text: The PRD covers the requirements rwb-integration owns (REQ-DRI-006, REQ-DRI-007, REQ-DRI-008 and REQ-DRI-013) and the one wave-2 orchestration step those requirements and the FSD carry; the consumer-side compositions assigned to the service in later wave story slices are not restated as P2 product requirements and are carried as open question Q-P2-06.
why: The FSD P2 serves four requirements, while the service story set also holds consumer-side contract slices whose requirements belong to other modules (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-8).
read: A composition that only calls other owners is a consumer of their baselines; its product requirements sit in their PRDs.
confirm: Product Owner with the solution architect
impact: If the boundary is drawn the other way, the PRD gains a capability per composition and the owning module PRD loses its scope statement.

text: Functions removed by D-RCV-35 keep their IDs in an exclusion table with their later home (ACE ingestion) and receive no functional requirement, no non-functional requirement and no acceptance criterion; no inbound adapter, inbound folder, inbound file check, inbound run record or sign-off exists in the target.
why: The FSD keeps the removed IDs without target behaviour (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-9) and the realignment must not restate a removed function as a requirement.
read: The removed rows are traceability anchors only.
impact: A reader who treats a removed row as a requirement would rebuild the inbound load.

text: The interface-level non-functional targets that no source states (largest file, records per file, daily tape volume, window length, extract size) inherit the programme targets that apply to every service and are held open under DL11 with the section R9 placeholder; no target is invented.
why: The BRD sizes the case store, the document hub and the decision log and nothing sizes an interface (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-11).
read: The only stated P2 measure is zero outbound items in the exception queue over one day.
impact: A missing target cannot be tested and stays a P2 gap until DL11 closes.

text: The debt buyer tape carries only the fields that the approved sale terms and the approved mask list allow, the mask list is a reference-data row owned by Compliance, and no field-level rule is fixed by this PRD.
why: NFR-041 masks the tape before the data room while the FSD allows the sale terms to pass personal data (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-12).
read: The rule is stated; the field list waits on DL26.
impact: An unmasked field in the tape is a reportable breach.

text: INT-17 (NSS), INT-18 (LINE OA) and INT-22 (PII Kafka, audit and SOC logs) remain ACE capabilities that the Workbench uses with no P2 build, no P2 adapter and no P2 requirement; their behaviour, retry and evidence are ACE's.
why: The three rows of the FSD register state ACE as the adapter and ACE as the retry and carry no Workbench behaviour (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-13).
read: The PRD states them as reused capabilities in the relationship-to-ACE section.
confirm: Solution architect with the ACE team lead
impact: A P2 build of these paths would duplicate ACE and breach the reuse rule.

text: The partner portal and the document hub keep their own contracts and their own transport (S9 rwb-partner and P5 rwb-document); rwb-integration carries no requirement for them and the FSD sentence that claims their transport is recorded as superseded.
why: Arch v5 slide 16 gives P2 two party file interfaces only, and slide 41 gives the partner and document capabilities to S9 and P5 (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-14).
read: A file that a partner or document flow needs is delivered through the same P2 capability, but the flow and its requirement belong to its owner.
impact: A claimed transport would put another service's traffic in the P2 baseline.

text: No earlier PRD exists in this document family, so this file is version 1 of Recovery Workbench PRD P2 rwb-integration and its section set follows the PRD Builder contract of the AI-SDLC playbook rather than a predecessor document.
why: The PRD folder is created by this work package and the family has no v0 file.
read: Nothing is copied from a predecessor; every section is built from the BRD, the FSD, Arch v5 and the Ownership Map.
impact: A later PRD version adds rows and does not change the section set.

text: The requirement IDs of this PRD are CAP-P2-nnn, FR-P2-nnn, NFR-P2-nnn and AC-P2-nnn, all new under D-RCV-60; every BRD requirement ID (REQ-DRI-nnn) and every BRD non-functional ID (NFR-nnn) is copied character for character and never renumbered.
why: The realignment adds a product layer above a BRD whose IDs must stay stable for traceability to the story set.
read: FR-P2-nnn maps to the FSD requirement IDs REQ-DRI-006, REQ-DRI-007, REQ-DRI-008 and REQ-DRI-013.
applied_in: Section 1 ID conventions, section 6, section 7, section 11
impact: A changed BRD ID breaks the trace to the story set and the change register.

text: The EFS hand-over intake is a P2 orchestration step in wave 2: it is started when the ACE batch for EFS is complete, runs once per business date, takes its per-account key before it asks rwb-case for the case, and calls the ledger append idempotently; the ACE reads themselves stay with rwb-source-data.
why: FSD P2 serves REQ-DRI-013 and the wave-2 contract story of the service fixes the step, while the BRD P2 section does not describe it.
read: The step is orchestration and idempotency, not data access; no ACE view and no ledger table belongs to P2.
confirm: Product Owner with the solution architect
impact: If the step is not P2's, the wave-2 capability leaves the PRD and REQ-DRI-013 has no P2 trace.

text: The retention period of an outbound item, a delivery record, a manifest and a transmission acknowledgement is open under DL26; the PRD requires only that the record of a send, an exception and a resend outlives the retention period of the case it belongs to.
why: No source sets a period for the P2 transmission records (CG-B-REQ-PRD-P2-15).
read: The rule is stated as a dependency on DL26, with the section R9 placeholder for the period.
impact: A purge before the case closes destroys the evidence of a send.
